subject: Observability add-ons — credit math & seat smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-ons — credit math & seat smoothing proposal

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for walking through the observability scope yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a simple credit model that shows two ways to structure the add-ons (retention + tracing + advanced dashboards) against Acme's expected usage profile. High level:

- Option A: Quarterly smoothing — a 3-month smoothing window, smaller monthly variance, lower overage risk.
- Option B: Annual commit + earnback credits — higher initial commitment, deeper price on month-of-commit, credits applied to overages later.

Can you confirm which cadence Procurement prefers (quarterly vs annual)? Also a couple of asks so we can finalize the commercial:

1) Is Acme comfortable with credits that are applied to metered overages only (not to base subscription)?
2) Do you need invoicing to reflect credits as a line-item (we can make them show as a negative charge)?

I've highlighted a sample concession in the sheet — a one-time onboarding credit equal to 30% of Q1 add-on spend (applied to Q1 invoices). That is an initial suggestion to smooth the price while you ramp.

Attachment: observability_credit_sheet_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

If it helps, happy to do a quick call with Procurement tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
[Attachment: observability_credit_sheet_v1.xlsx]

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — credit math & seat smoothing proposal

Kim — appreciate the model, that helps a lot. A few points from Procurement and Finance after a quick review:

- Procurement preference: quarterly smoothing is preferred (simpler for our OPS team).
- Credits: Finance wants credits to show as a separate line item on invoices and prefers they apply to the invoice month (not retrospective adjustments).
- Pricing ask: given our volume growth profile, we're asking for a year-one effective discount of 20% on the advanced dashboards SKU if we commit to the quarterly smoothing path.

I've attached a counter-proposal with a blended effective rate and a column for expected month-by-month usage to show where the overage hits are likely to occur.

Attachment: acme_counter_proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)

Can you confirm whether credits applied at invoice-time are compatible with Redwood's billing system? If not, we may need a manual ledger entry — not ideal for us.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Operations, Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_counter_proposal.xlsx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Observability add-ons — credit math & seat smoothing proposal

Ben / Markus — forwarding Acme's counter-proposal. Key asks: quarterly smoothing (OK), credits must appear as invoice line items and they are requesting a year-one effective 20% discount on advanced dashboards if we accept the smoothing.

My read:
- Quarterly smoothing is operationally straightforward and reduces overage friction.
- Showing credits on the invoice is doable, but we need billing to confirm whether credits are processed automatically (invoice-level negative line) or via a separate credit memo/ledger entry.
- The 20% year-one ask is material; I suggested a compromise in-thread in the attached sheet (one-time onboarding smoothing credit at 30% of Q1 add-on spend plus a 10% ongoing discount on dashboards for Q1–Q2 only) — that nets below 20% effective for year one in most ramp scenarios and buys us margin back in Q3.

Requests:
1) Markus — can Billing confirm if invoice-line credit display is supported and whether we need to issue credit memos instead? Also flag any accounting constraints for recognizing credits monthly.
2) Ben — do you have authority to approve the proposed split (onboarding credit + temporary 10% dashboard discount), or would this require Revenue/Deals sign-off?

I attached the original sheet with my colored assumptions.

Thanks,
Kim
[Quoted message attached]
[Attachment: observability_credit_sheet_v1.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability add-ons — credit math & seat smoothing proposal

Kim / Markus — good summary. I approve a commercial path that should land the deal while protecting margin. Details below:

Decision & commercial structure
- Accept quarterly smoothing as the operational cadence.
- Approve a one-time onboarding credit equal to 30% of Acme's projected Q1 add-on spend (applied as an invoice-line credit on each of the Q1 invoices until the credit is exhausted).
- Offer an additional temporary 10% discount on the advanced dashboards SKU for Q1 and Q2 only.
- Do not extend a headline 20% full-year discount. The combination above should be competitive and reversible at renewal.

Billing / accounting notes (Markus)
- Markus: please confirm technical feasibility. Preferred approach: negative-line invoice entries (automatic) that reduce the invoice total and flow through as normal credit line items. If the billing system cannot render automated negative-line items, issue monthly credit memos that reference the invoice number. Either way, mark credits as 'Onboarding Credit — ACME-2026-Q2-OBS-01' for audit.

Next steps
1) Kimberly: update the pricing sheet to reflect the approved structure and produce a sample invoice for May (first month with credits applied). Attach the sample and send to Olivia + Procurement.
2) Markus: confirm billing approach and any lag to automate negative-line credits.
3) Kimberly: if Procurement requires, loop in Legal for a short amendment or SOW addendum.

Attachment: approved_credit_calc_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: approved_credit_calc_v1.xlsx]
